newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Curve flattens on wages.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Curve flattens on wages.

text.p: The Australian bond yield curve flattened sharply after the release of a stronger than expected first quarter wages report which reduced hopes of any early cut in official interest rates and prompted talk of a tightening.

"Watch for a flatter yield curve as the rate hike is priced into the market, while the long end holds on the back of a market friendly Budget and signs that near term inflation will be low," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia.
The Federal budget will be handed down on May 13.

The three-/10-year bond yield futures spread dropped to its lowest level since early April following the first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings data, which showed a 1.3 percent rise for 4.6 percent year-on-year, above the Reserve Bank's 4.5 percent comfort zone.

Yield spread differentials also blew out sharply against the dollar bloc on the data with the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread widening to 120 basis points, making a clean break of resistance at 110 basis points.
The U.S. market rallied on Wednesday, taking a stronger than expected first quarter GDP in its stride, and pinning hopes on an early balanced budget agreement in Washington.

Canadian bonds continued to rebound after its recent underperformance against the bloc, while New Zealand bonds weakened on reported comments by RBNZ governor Don Brash that the central bank would need to review at some stage whether its
assumed line of monetary conditions was appropriate.
However, N.Z. debt still outperformed Australia on the day with the 10-year spread between the two going to a discount from a premium in New Zealand's favour.
